$comment: The review team runs these against the live plugin, so every positive case must reproducibly succeed and every negative case must reproducibly NOT invoke the plugin. Exactly five positive and three negative, the portal's minimum. `tools_triggered` is the exact MCP tool name. Descriptions and expected outputs are review-facing: what the reviewer sees, never how the server does it. Reviewer notes that used to live in a separate prompts file are folded into the descriptions here, because this file is what the portal imports.

positive.description: Single-file deploy, the simplest path. The model writes one index.html and deploys it with no account, no confirmation gate and no setup; the deploy card renders inline. The screenshot tile may read "Preview loading" for up to about thirty seconds while the capture lands.
positive.user_prompt: Deploy a single-page website that says "Hello world" in big bold text.
positive.expected_output: A deploy card with a live *.shipstatic.com URL, "1 file" and a small byte count, a screenshot of the page, and a "Claim to keep forever" link. Opening the URL shows the Hello world page.

positive.description: Multi-file site with cross-links. The model generates index.html, styles.css and about.html and sends all three in ONE deploy call; the stylesheet applies and the about link works on the live site.
positive.user_prompt: Build me a landing page for a fictional coffee shop called "Blackbird Coffee" with an index.html, a styles.css file, and a small about.html page. Deploy it.
positive.expected_output: A deploy card showing "3 files". The URL opens a styled landing page and its About link opens /about.html.

positive.description: Deterministic content the reviewer can verify with a single fetch of the URL. The model must use the exact heading and title text and must echo the deployment URL in its reply.
positive.user_prompt: Deploy an HTML page whose <h1> reads exactly "Hello reviewer" and whose <title> reads "ShipStatic test". Then tell me the URL.
positive.expected_output:
A deploy card and the URL repeated in the reply. Fetching the URL returns HTML containing exactly

Hello reviewer

and ShipStatic test.

positive.description: Password-protected deploy. The model passes the password with the deploy and repeats it back to the user, since a password the user never sees locks them out. The card shows a lock chip and the site asks for the password before rendering.
positive.user_prompt: Deploy a one-page "coming soon" landing page and protect it with the password "demo123".
positive.expected_output: A deploy card with a lock chip in its meta row, the password "demo123" confirmed in the reply, and a URL that prompts for the password before showing the page.

positive.description: An account feature, exercising the sign-in the plugin offers on demand. Listing needs a connected ShipStatic account, so the first call prompts the user to connect; signing in sends a magic link to the address the reviewer enters (a free account is created on first sign-in). After connecting, the list returns.
positive.expected_output: Without a connected account, ChatGPT offers to connect ShipStatic and opens the sign-in. Once connected, the reply lists the account's deployments with their URLs (an empty list for a fresh account), and later deploys in the same conversation land in that account.

negative.description: An unrelated productivity request. Nothing about publishing a site; the plugin must not be invoked.
negative.user_prompt: What meetings do I have tomorrow?
negative.expected_output: ChatGPT answers from its own tools or says it cannot see a calendar. ShipStatic is not called and no deploy card appears.

negative.description: A nearby question that needs an explanation, not a deployment. The plugin's domain tools return DNS records for a domain the user owns on ShipStatic; a general question about DNS should be answered in prose without calling them.
negative.user_prompt: Can you explain what a CNAME record is and how it differs from an A record?
negative.expected_output: A plain explanation of the two record types. No ShipStatic tool is called and nothing is deployed.

negative.description: A hosting request the plugin cannot serve. ShipStatic hosts static sites only; a server process is out of scope, so the model should say so rather than deploy something that cannot run.
negative.user_prompt: Deploy my Node.js Express API server with its PostgreSQL database so it runs 24/7.
negative.expected_output: ChatGPT explains that ShipStatic hosts static sites (HTML, CSS, JavaScript and assets) and cannot run a server or a database, and suggests what would fit instead. No deploy is attempted and no card appears.
